gen-gf-gugi-work-sans: Distinctive is Gugi, with a tall lowercase that nearly reaches its capitals. Work Sans sits beside it in a modern, contemporary mood, its tidy sans letters making the heading feel louder and the pairing livelier.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-fs-asap: Ascenders barely clear the x-height in Love Ya Like A Sister. It brings bold, expressive character to a line, while Asap, a readable sans with open arcs, handles the steady work of carrying words.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-piazzolla: Tight chain links: New Title locks its bold letters together, tall lowercase towering over the capitals. And Piazzolla brings classic serif refinement, its e opened wide, and lets paragraphs unfold with authority.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-be-vietna: Alien Encounters spaces its letter pairs far apart, a high x-height giving the heading an otherworldly, technological feel. Be Vietnam Pro reads smoothly beneath it, its sans strokes bent like steel rod with no stress in any curve.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads crisp, its plain sans curves open at both ends. What stands out is the temperament gap: Azonix commands from above, while Fira Sans simply carries the words.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-merriweather-sans: Commanding is Bloody, with big round lowercase bowls that fill every single word with weight and drama. Merriweather Sans keeps paragraphs sturdy, each e open to the right.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-fs-supreme: Supreme lays a thick, heavy-looking strip of crisp text through the middle, its letters held open rather than curled shut. Bushcraft, closed and widely spaced, supplies the artistic flourish.
gen-dafont-college-general-sans: College gives every curve the weight of its stems, with big counters inside a tall lowercase. General Sans, a smooth sans-serif, then lets its steady pen pressure carry the lines the heading starts.
gen-dafont-conthrax-manrope: Wide and geometric: Conthrax stretches its lowercase a open, with bodies so tall the capitals barely rise above them. Manrope joins it with bright, open curves and a friendly line.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-epilogue: Disorder runs raw and chaotic, its glyphs set well apart and its high x-height making lowercase look big. But Epilogue, a wiry monoline sans, is the one that carries the text, with curvy, unclamped letters.
